summary: Attacked the extraction of Harpaz-Wittenberg, 'The Massey vanishing conjecture for number fields' (Duke Math. J. 172 (2023), 1-41), re-fetched and hashed to the recorded SHA-256. The 158 items, the 21 cited TauCeti declarations, the 8 cited roadmap stages, both Part II proposals and the routing graph are sound, and the record's zero sourceIssues is consistent with the paper, which is clean at every cross-reference checked. One finding: the same statement, the Picard group of a finite-stabilizer homogeneous space, is proposed as a missing item twice into one roadmap, once here and once by PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20, although that record's own route reason says not to make a second copy of exactly this interface.
checked: The source, re-fetched from https://www.math.univ-paris13.fr/~wittenberg/globalmassey.pdf and hashed to d95100ebd7210600873351ffbe1f3f1dc0fd3f36b815ca70286884801afc546f, 33 pages, matching the hash the record's source block records; the PDF is not stamped, so the hash reproduces.

Every one of the 21 tauceti: declarations the items cite, at the pinned commit (Tau Ceti f790474, Mathlib 082e2d3): all 21 exist. Two were read in full: explicitCup11, whose cochain formula is (a cup b)(g,h) = mu(a g)(g . b h) as item 10 states, and commutator_superdiagonalSubgroup_le : [U^r, U^s] <= U^(r+s), which agrees with item 12 once the paper's U_0 = U indexing is matched to the pin's, which starts at 1.

All 8 roadmap stages cited by the planned items exist as stage ids in the atlas extracts (ProfiniteCohomology layers 6, 9, 10; ClassFieldTheory layers 5, 10; DGAInfinity layer 8; ProfiniteProPGroups layer 5; ModularCurves 0d).

Item statements against the paper at their locators, sampled across the record: item 96 against Theorem 1.3, item 26 against the construction of the splitting variety in section 2 (N = |U| + 1, V = (SL_N x T_alpha)/U at (2.2), geometric stabilizer U_1), item 33 against the definition of the geometric stabilizer and its outer action in section 2, items 14, 15, 16 against the unitriangular group of section 1.

Both Part II proposals: each title is an exact prefix extension of its parent's atlas title as section 15 requires, and both roadmap ids are free. ProfiniteCohomologyPartIIMasseyGalois extends 'Continuous cohomology of profinite groups'; HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey extends 'Heights, rational points and obstructions'.
The routing graph: all 133 missing items are routed, each exactly once; no route's items array repeats an id; the parent and prerequisite edges are acyclic.
Section 16's API and test requirement on every missing definition and construction: all 48 carry both an API list and a Tests list.

Coverage of the paper's numbered statements: 42 of 45 are carried by an item. The three that are not are Conjecture 1.1, whose content item 96 states in full rather than by reference; Remark 1.2, which is expository; and Remark 2.7, whose base-point independence is carried by item 33 as an API contract and as a test, with Remark 2.7's own transport formula (g, sigma) -> (r g sigma(r)^-1, sigma) written out. None of the three is an omission.
Whether items 2 to 5 duplicate mathematics the atlas already plans: they are planned at DGAInfinity layer 8, which is the correct import, not a duplication.

The paper itself for slips, as a check on the record's empty sourceIssues: internal cross-references and doubled words are clean; the three apparent numbering mismatches are citations of other papers, not internal references. The empty sourceIssues is right.

The 133 missing items against the pinned declarations index, for mathematics the libraries already have: no missing item is already in the library. The near cases were checked individually. Item 14 (elementary transvections) already directs reuse of TauCeti.transvectionUnit, and what it adds beyond Mathlib's Matrix.transvection and SpecialLinearGroup.transvection, the unique ordered product expansion and the commutator formulas by index case, is genuinely absent from both libraries. Item 15 is right to ask for the reverse inclusions: [U,U] = U^1 and [U^1,U^1] = U^3 in the paper's indexing are sharper than the library's [U^r,U^s] <= U^(r+s), and are correct, since the bracket of the degree->=2 part of the Lie algebra lands in degree >= 4. Bogomolov multipliers (item 50) and the unramified Brauer group (item 29) appear nowhere in the index.

Every item of this record against the items of every other PAPER-*.result.json in the repository, by name and by statement, for mathematics planned twice; then, for the one roadmap this record shares with another, a statement-level comparison of all 44 items it routes there against all 54 that PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20 routes there. Exactly one pair collides, which is the finding below; the rest of the shared roadmap is disjoint.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23.result.json, item PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/39, and its route to HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey
findings.claim: The Picard group of a finite-stabilizer homogeneous space is proposed as a missing item twice into the same roadmap. Item PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/39 and item PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/81 carry the same name and the same statement, both have status missing, and both are routed into HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey, with the same parent HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions and the same route kind part-ii. Neither record's coalescence block is populated, so nothing in the data records that the two are one statement, and a worker building that roadmap from these two records would plan and formalise it twice or have to adjudicate the ownership by hand.
findings.evidence: PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/39, a construction, locator 'section 3 p.8': 'In characteristic zero, for semisimple simply connected G and homogeneous V with finite geometric stabilizer H, Pic(V_kbar)=Hom(H^ab,kbar*)=Hom(H^ab,mu_inf), equivariantly for Gamma_k.' PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/81, a theorem, locator 'section 5 p.18': 'In the setup of section 5, Pic(V_kbar) is canonically Hom(H^ab,kbar*), equivariantly for Gamma_k. Use Kummer, constant units and the geometric fundamental group; the character action includes the action on roots of unity.' The two agree: H is finite, so Hom(H^ab, kbar*) = Hom(H^ab, mu_inf). That the copy is unintended is stated in the other record itself. The reason on PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20's route to this roadmap reads: 'Reuse the same candidate owner proposed in PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23 for its HW20 Theorem B input. ... This paper supplies the general homogeneous-space foundation required by that candidate; do not create another copy of the supersolvable theorem or finite-stabilizer Picard/Brauer interfaces.' That discipline was applied to the supersolvable theorem, whose item in PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20 carries the note 'This is the same HW20 input already requested by PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23; the shared candidate owner below receives the proof once', and it was not applied to the Picard interface named in the same sentence.
findings.fix: Consolidate onto PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/81 and drop PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/39 from this record's route to HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey, recording the identification the way the other records record shared ownership, with a coalescence entry naming PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/81 as the owner and this item as a consumer. HW20 is the right owner on both grounds the route reasons already give: it is the paper that proves the statement, in its section 5, and its route declares itself the complete homogeneous-space foundation for this shared roadmap, while this paper only consumes the result. Nothing is lost by consolidating and nothing is orphaned: the two statements agree, the items here that depend on the Picard identification stay in the same roadmap and can cite the surviving item, and if the mu_inf form or the construction framing of item 39 is wanted it should be folded into PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/81's statement and API note. If instead the maintainers prefer this record to keep the item, the same fix applies with the roles reversed, but then PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20's route reason should stop forbidding the second copy.
